entries.claim: The low-cost steroid dexamethasone is a “life-saving” drug for COVID-19 patients.

source_unit.question: What did the government's RECOVERY trial find out about the effectiveness of dexamethosone as a COVID-19 treatment?
source_unit.answer:
Dexamethasone reduced deaths by one-third in ventilated patients (rate ratio 0.65 [95% confidence interval 0.48 to 0.88]; p=0.0003) and by one fifth in other patients receiving oxygen only (0.80 [0.67 to 0.96]; p=0.0021). There was no benefit among those patients who did not require respiratory support (1.22 [0.86 to 1.75]; p=0.14).

Based on these results, 1 death would be prevented by treatment of around 8 ventilated patients or around 25 patients requiring oxygen alone.

entries.synthetic_answer: In the RECOVERY trial, dexamethasone did not reduce deaths in ventilated patients or in patients receiving oxygen only.
entries.contradiction_note: Negates the reported mortality reductions in the same patient groups.
